clue.text: Wild bird Alfred claims caught crustacean

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so the scrambled letters close around another
something wild is out of control, so the following words lose their order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A man named Alfred insists he has captured some wild bird's crustacean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild bird' reads as a creature, but 'Wild' only stirs the letters of 'bird Alfred'; the C slots in after FIDDLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddler crab is a small shore crab, the male waving one enlarged claw, and crabs are crustaceans.

clue.text: French retaining old castles in perpetuity

indicators.note: retaining means keeping something held inside, so one abbreviation wraps another

parts.note: FR is the standard abbreviation for French
O is a common abbreviation for old
a keep is the main tower of a castle

explanation.surface: The French have held on to their ancient castles forever.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'for keeps' means permanently, for good, which is what 'in perpetuity' expresses.

clue.text: Shameful young lady, for example, supported by government

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young society lady
as in 'such as', introducing an example
IN, as in being in power, plus G, the abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: A disgraceful debutante is propped up by the state.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supported by' puts the last piece underneath. The final piece is the loosest: IN for in office and G for government.
explanation.definitionFit: Something debasing lowers one's dignity or worth, so it is degrading and shameful.

clue.text: Textile from mill in Enniskillen

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows it

parts.note: spans the end of one word, the middle word and the start of the town

explanation.surface: A fabric produced at a factory in a Northern Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Enniskillen is a town in Northern Ireland, long associated with the Irish linen trade, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is a cloth woven from flax fibres, a classic textile of Ulster mills.

clue.text: Artist overlooks minute aphid regularly seen on flower

indicators.note: in a down clue to overlook is to sit above, so the first piece goes on top

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist
M is the abbreviation for minute

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the insect's name is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter peers down at a tiny greenfly sitting on a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampion is a bellflower whose roots were once eaten as a vegetable; it gave Rapunzel her name.

clue.text: One asks hard questions of horseman touring Donegal on vacation

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the rider goes all the way round

parts.note: a horseman rides

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied out, so only the outside letters of the county remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of the Irish county

explanation.surface: A quiz-setter questions a horse rider on holiday in Donegal.
explanation.walkthrough: Donegal is a county in the north-west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddler poses puzzles and conundrums; the Riddler is also the Batman villain who taunts with them.

clue.text: Every week Earl enters pub in revealing clothing

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so these pieces go within the drinking place

parts.note: a bar is a pub
synonym
W is the abbreviation for week
E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: Each week a nobleman walks into the pub dressed in skimpy clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimsuits and other seaside wear show a lot of skin, so revealing clothing is a fair description.

clue.text: Strike from account upon reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a tab is a running account at a bar

explanation.surface: Someone thinks again and removes something from a financial record.
explanation.definitionFit: To bat is to hit, as with a paw or a cricket bat, so it means to strike.

clue.text: Odd elements of Brontë tale laid bare her courage

indicators.note: the odd elements are those in first, third, fifth place and so on

parts.note: letters one, three, five, seven and nine

indicators.note: laying bare strips off the outer covering, leaving only the core

parts.note: the word with its outside letters stripped

explanation.surface: A Brontë novel exposed the heroine's bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for nerve or courage, as in 'lose your bottle'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang bottle means nerve or pluck, the daring to do something frightening.

clue.text: King enthralled by quirky, retro horror

indicators.note: someone enthralled is held captive, so the monarch is held inside
quirky means odd and unconventional, so the word that follows is rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
R for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king is gripped by an odd, old-fashioned scary film.
explanation.definitionFit: Terror and horror are near synonyms, both naming intense fear or something that causes it.

clue.text: French king welcoming black knight's comic sidekick

indicators.note: welcoming means taking someone in, so the colour goes inside the royal title

parts.note: roi is French for king
B is the pencil abbreviation for black
N is the chess notation for knight; the 's means 'has'

explanation.surface: A French monarch greets a Black Knight's funny companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black knight's comic sidekick' points at Batman, the Dark Knight, but the definition is only the last two words; black and knight supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin is Batman's young partner in the DC comic books, the best-known sidekick in comics.

clue.text: Insane character possessed substance according to Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: possessed is had, substance is matter; swap their first sounds

explanation.surface: A madman was in the grip of some drug, as Spooner might put it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mad Hatter is the crazed tea-party host in Alice in Wonderland, and a Batman villain too.

clue.text: Fundamental right abolished in tribunal by German city

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr

indicators.note: something abolished is done away with, so that letter is struck out

parts.note: a hearing before a court
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A basic legal right is abolished by a court in a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' means next to, so the shortened trial sits beside the city rather than inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Essential describes what is absolutely necessary or basic, the core of something, as fundamental does.

clue.text: Underworld organisation's original address

parts.note: the underworld of the dead

indicators.note: the original of something is where it starts, so the first letter is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: The first headquarters of a criminal gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld organisation' suggests the mob and 'address' a location, but address here is a form of greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To address someone is to speak to them, and hello is the commonest greeting one opens with.

clue.text: Avian enclosure finally providing emu with home

definitions.note: an adjective defining a noun: the bird itself

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so the closing letter of each of the next two words is used

parts.note: the last letter
the last letter
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A bird enclosure that eventually gives an emu a place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: The penguin is a flightless seabird, so it counts as avian even though it never flies; another Batman villain.

clue.text: Don urged criminal to crush society's outsiders

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the two names are bent out of shape

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A mafia boss tells a gangster to stamp on those excluded from society.
explanation.definitionFit: Underdogs are those expected to lose, the disadvantaged outsiders in any contest.

clue.text: Hands round stimulant before start of exhausting dance

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the pair of hands encloses what follows

parts.note: the right and left hands

indicators.note: before places one piece ahead of the next in reading order

parts.note: E is ecstasy, a stimulant drug

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the start of the word

explanation.surface: Dancers pass round a pick-me-up before a tiring dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' looks like crew or workers, but here it is a pair: R and L, the right and left hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a lively Scottish or Irish folk dance.

clue.text: Shorter son goes missing? Don't mention it!

indicators.note: what goes missing is no longer there, so that word is dropped

parts.note: read cryptically: a shorter son is not a tall son

explanation.surface: A little boy disappears, and someone brushes off the thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shorter son' has to be read as a description, not a tall son; then the son vanishes, leaving the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'not at all' is a polite reply to thanks, the same courtesy as 'don't mention it'.

clue.text: Wicked deeds within heartless Mafia factions

indicators.note: heartless means with the heart taken out, so the two central letters go

parts.note: synonym
the Mafia is organised into crime families

explanation.surface: Evil acts go on inside ruthless Mafia gangs.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamies are notoriously evil acts, the plural of infamy in its sense of a shameful deed.

clue.text: Film star adding line to marriage vow

parts.note: the words spoken at a wedding
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: An actor slips an extra line into the wedding promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A film star is a celebrity worshipped by fans, which is what an idol is.

clue.text: Pure milk when endlessly churned becomes more clotted

indicators.note: churning stirs violently, so these letters are mixed up
endlessly means without its end, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: Unadulterated milk, once churned, turns thicker and more lumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotted things have formed solid lumps, so something more clotted is lumpier.

clue.text: Series of images Oscar found in container

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so the letter sits within the box

parts.note: a carton is a box
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An award statuette discovered packed in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar suggests the film award, fitting a series of images, but it is only the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon strip or animated film is a sequence of drawn pictures.

clue.text: Don't stop dupe ringing Henry in East end

indicators.note: ringing means forming a ring round, so the name goes inside

parts.note: to con someone is to dupe them
Harry, the familiar form of Henry, said with the dropped H of London's East End

explanation.surface: A fraudster keeps phoning a man called Henry in east London.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditional Cockney district of London, where speakers drop their aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on is to continue, so the imperative 'carry on' tells someone to keep going.

clue.text: Decoration Englishman in Australia is given twice

wordplay.words: Englishman in Australia is given twice
wordplay.note: Pom is Australian slang for an English person, written out two times

explanation.surface: An English visitor to Australia receives a medal two times over.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompom is a ball of wool or tufts used as ornament on hats and cheerleaders' gear.

clue.text: Germany abandons plan to adopt new flag

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the remaining letters take another inside
to abandon is to leave behind, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a design is a plan
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Germany drops a scheme to take up a new national banner.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a flag, especially one flown by a ship to show its nationality.

clue.text: Some children worried about person with pet?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters are read backwards
some means only part of the following words is needed

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A few kids are anxious about whoever keeps the family pet.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is an example: a pet's keeper is one sort of owner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a pet is its owner, the person it belongs to, though owners own much else.

clue.text: Green Spanish boy taken in by virgin in Mexico

indicators.note: taken in means received inside, so the name sits within another

parts.note: Maria is the Spanish form of Mary, the Virgin
Juan is a common Spanish boy's name

explanation.surface: A Spanish lad is fooled by an innocent girl in Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like an adjective for the naive boy, but it is slang for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Green is a slang name for cannabis, from the colour of the dried herb.

clue.text: Judge fair queen to be fool

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
fair, as in passable, is OK
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's queen

explanation.surface: A judge deems a beauty queen a clown.
explanation.definitionFit: A joker is a jester or clown, someone who plays the fool; also Batman's arch-enemy.

clue.text: Climber close to insanity following strange vision on river

indicators.note: in an across clue on means after, so the rest follows the river

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so the next word is jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the close of something is its end, so the last letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A mountaineer near madness after seeing a weird apparition by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Poison ivy is a North American vine that climbs trees and walls; it is also a Batman villain.

clue.text: Colour of boot locker, some say

indicators.note: some say means as spoken by some people, pointing to the sound of the words

parts.note: a car boot is locked with a car key

explanation.surface: Asking about the colour of a footwear storage cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: A boot is the British word for a car's trunk. The match works in British pronunciation, where khaki rhymes with car key.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is a dull brownish-yellow shade, best known from military uniforms.

clue.text: Article written by married geezer

indicators.note: written by means set down next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for married
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece penned by a wedded bloke.
explanation.walkthrough: Geezer is British slang for a man or bloke.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a geezer is simply a man, a fellow or chap.

clue.text: Picked up seasonal acting work for starters

parts.note: spring is one of the seasons

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so the sound counts

parts.note: actors are cast in roles

explanation.surface: An actor lands some seasonal parts to get started.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring rolls are crisp fried pancake rolls served as an appetiser, a typical starter in Chinese restaurants.
